title: Applying the Sandwich (Squeeze) Theorem
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Prove using the Sandwich Theorem that lim_{x -> 0} x^2 sin(1/x) = 0.

steps.title: Bound the Sine Function
steps.explanation: Recall that the range of the sine function is bounded strictly within [-1, 1].
steps.why: The sine function is bounded for all real arguments regardless of how rapidly the argument oscillates.

steps.title: Multiply the Inequality by x^2
steps.explanation: Multiply through by x^2. Since x^2 > 0 for all x != 0, the inequality directions are preserved.
steps.why: Multiplying an inequality by a strictly positive quantity maintains the order of inequalities.

steps.title: Evaluate the Limits of the Bounding Functions
steps.explanation: Both the lower bound -x^2 and upper bound x^2 converge to 0 as x -> 0.
steps.why: Direct substitution into the quadratic bounding functions gives zero.

steps.title: Conclude via the Sandwich Theorem
steps.explanation: Because the middle function is trapped between bounds converging to 0, it must also converge to 0.
steps.why: Statement and conclusion of the Sandwich (Squeeze) Theorem.
